scenarios.title: Unable to Reach the Activation Service

environment.gpu: Intel Iris Xe + NVIDIA RTX 3050 Laptop
environment.network: Corporate wired LAN; Always-On VPN and web proxy required
environment.av: CrowdStrike Falcon + corporate proxy SSL inspection
environment.notes: Business license. Customer pasted a 25-character key. Error: Unable to Reach the Activation Service. Official source: Camtasia Editor for Windows Activation Messages.

scenarios.summary: Camtasia 2026.2.1 will not activate on the corporate network. The customer sees Unable to Reach the Activation Service after pasting their business software key.
scenarios.description:
Hi Support,

I just installed Camtasia 2026.2.1 on my work laptop and entered our software key. I keep getting:

  Unable to Reach the Activation Service

I am on the office network with VPN connected (required by IT). I can browse the web. Please activate this today — I have a course recording this afternoon.

Thanks,
Jordan Hale
Northwind Learning
scenarios.crashLog:
Activation dialog: Unable to Reach the Activation Service
License type: 25-character business/perpetual key
Network: Always-On VPN + corporate proxy

Official guidance (do not invent a workaround):
https://support.techsmith.com/hc/en-us/articles/360041856891-Camtasia-Editor-for-Windows-Activation-Messages

Documented causes besides being offline: VPNs, proxy servers, and firewalls.
Documented first test: disconnect the VPN just long enough to activate, then reconnect.
If the PC is truly offline, use Offline Activation (same article).
Do not invent a new software key.

sources.title: Camtasia Editor for Windows Activation Messages
Find, Enter, or Recover Your Software Key (Snagit & Camtasia)

diagnosticSteps.prompt: The customer pasted a 25-character key and got Unable to Reach the Activation Service. What does TechSmith document as the meaning of that message?

options.label: The PC cannot reach TechSmith’s activation service — no internet, or a VPN, proxy, or firewall is blocking it.
options.feedback: Matches the Activation Messages article: the machine is offline or something is blocking the activation service. Documented non-offline causes are VPNs, proxy servers, and firewalls.

options.label: Treat this as Key Doesn't Match Version and have them download a different Camtasia build.
options.feedback: Key Doesn't Match Version is a different message in the same article; this ticket is a connectivity block, not a version mismatch.

options.label: Treat this as Installation Limit Reached and tell them the key already has two activations.
options.feedback: Installation Limit Reached is a separate message in the Activation Messages article; this error is about reaching the service, not seat count.

options.label: Treat this as Activation Failed: Invalid Date/Time and have them correct the Windows clock first.
options.feedback: Invalid Date/Time is documented in the same article, but this ticket quotes Unable to Reach the Activation Service, which is VPN, proxy, or firewall.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: What is the documented first test for a VPN user who cannot reach the activation service?

options.label: Ask them to disconnect the VPN just long enough to activate Camtasia, then reconnect afterward.
options.feedback: Exact guidance from the Activation Messages article: for a VPN, disconnect just to activate, then connect again without issue after activation.

options.label: Treat this as Invalid Key and have them copy a different key from the Keys tab, without testing VPN or proxy connectivity.
options.feedback: This message is a reachability problem, not Invalid Key; keys come from manage.techsmith.com or the receipt, and swapping keys will not open the activation service.

options.label: Have them delete Identity and Reginfo.ini under ProgramData\TechSmith\Camtasia Studio 20, which is the documented fix for You Must Sign In, not this connectivity error.
options.feedback: That path is documented for You Must Sign In or Enter a Software Key, not for Unable to Reach the Activation Service. Use it only if the message matches.

options.label: Treat the VPN error as an expired license and send them to billing to repurchase Camtasia 2026.
options.feedback: Unable to Reach the Activation Service is a connectivity issue; the article does not treat it as a dead license or a repurchase.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: If they cannot disconnect VPN (Always-On) and still cannot activate, what stays inside official guidance?

options.label: Work with IT on proxy/firewall access to the activation service, or complete Offline Activation if the PC cannot reach the service.
options.feedback: The article names proxy servers and firewalls, points to proxy-activation steps, and says offline PCs need Offline Activation.

options.label: Have them delete Identity and Reginfo.ini as if this were You Must Sign In, instead of working with IT on proxy or firewall access or using Offline Activation.
options.feedback: Identity and Reginfo.ini are documented for You Must Sign In, not for Unable to Reach the Activation Service; stay on proxy, firewall, or Offline Activation.

options.label: Have them sign in with a personal TechSmith account so they can skip the business key on the corporate network.
options.feedback: This is a business-key install blocked by VPN, proxy, or firewall; Individual sign-in is not the documented fix for that message.

options.label: Also remind them they can confirm the key on the Keys tab at manage.techsmith.com if they need to re-copy it later.
options.feedback: True for finding keys, but it does not fix Unable to Reach the Activation Service. Keep it as a secondary note after connectivity.

emailCriteria.tone: Calm and specific. Name the exact error. Do not invent a new key or a hidden activation server list.
requiredElements: Name the error Unable to Reach the Activation Service
Documented causes: offline, VPN, proxy, or firewall
First test: disconnect VPN just to activate, then reconnect
If Always-On VPN: IT must allow activation traffic, or use Offline Activation
Link the official Activation Messages article
modelReplyHints: Quote the documented meaning of Unable to Reach the Activation Service.
Give the VPN disconnect-to-activate test first.
If they cannot drop VPN, stay on proxy/firewall or Offline Activation — do not invent IPs.

correct: Unable to Connect to Activation Server Error
acceptable: Camtasia Editor :: Activating Subscriptions :: Unable to Sign-in
expectedMacros.rationale: Business-key activation is blocked by VPN/proxy/firewall. Tag the connectivity error, not a subscription sign-in or a missing-key request.

environment.notes: Receipt in the ticket shows an Individual subscription (Create), not a perpetual/business key. Official source: Find, Enter, or Recover Your Software Key.

Hello,

I purchased Camtasia Create yesterday. The installer keeps asking me to sign in OR enter a software key. Please send my 25-character key (XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX) to this email so I can paste it in.

Sam Chen
scenarios.crashLog:
License type on file: Camtasia Individual subscription (Create)
Customer request: email a 25-character software key

https://support.techsmith.com/hc/en-us/articles/45434990817677-Find-Enter-or-Recover-Your-Software-Key-Snagit-Camtasia

options.label: Ask them to sign in at manage.techsmith.com and open the Keys tab, or read the key from Help > About or the original purchase receipt.

options.label: After signing in, they can confirm licensing under Help > About Camtasia.
options.feedback: Help > About is documented for confirming activation. Lead with Sign In using the purchase email.

emailCriteria.tone: Clear and reassuring. Individual subscriptions do not get a 25-character key.

Sign in with the purchase email
manage.techsmith.com Keys tab is for licenses that actually have keys
Do not invent or paste a sample key

Tell them to Sign In with the purchase email.
Point perpetual/business customers to manage.techsmith.com → Keys.

scenarios.title: Camtasia canvas is black — media won’t display

environment.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop, Game Ready 551.23
environment.notes: Timeline has media; canvas is black (or shows the desktop instead of the clip). Official source: Black Screen in Camtasia Editor Canvas.

scenarios.summary: The Camtasia Editor canvas is black even though clips are on the timeline. Preview of the feature (canvas playback) is not working.
scenarios.description:
The canvas in Camtasia is just black. I can see the clips on the timeline and I can hear audio, but the picture never shows. Sometimes I see my Windows desktop in the canvas instead of the recording. This started after a Windows update. Feature is broken — I cannot edit.

Riley Okonkwo
Adventure Works Media
scenarios.crashLog:
Symptom: canvas black / artifacts / desktop shown instead of timeline media
GPU: NVIDIA RTX 4060 Laptop (hybrid with Intel)
Camtasia 2026.2.1

Official article:
https://support.techsmith.com/hc/en-us/articles/231545347-Black-Screen-in-Camtasia-Editor-Canvas

Documented order:
1) Update the video card drivers (OEM or NVIDIA/AMD/Intel).
2) Windows Settings > System > Display > Graphics → add CamtasiaStudio.exe (Camtasia 2026 folder) → GPU Preference High Performance.
3) Edit > Preferences > Advanced → Hardware Acceleration → Microsoft Basic Render Driver, then close and reopen Camtasia.

Do not invent encoder error codes that are not in this ticket.

scenarios.title: Who is using our Camtasia seats?

environment.app: Camtasia Business subscription — volume key deploy
environment.notes: Admin wants a portal list of who activated Camtasia. Official answer: there is no activation audit portal for Snagit/Camtasia. Seat management exists only for Assets, Audiate, and Screencast Pro.

scenarios.summary: University IT wants to see license count / who is using Camtasia Business activations in the TechSmith portal.
scenarios.description:
We purchased a Camtasia Business subscription for the faculty. I am the admin. Please send a report of:
1) How many seats are in use
2) Which email addresses are assigned
3) How I can reclaim a seat when a professor leaves

I expected this under manage.techsmith.com seat management, like our Screencast Pro seats.

Avery Kim
Litware University IT
scenarios.crashLog:
Intent: License Count.
Product: Camtasia Business (software key / not named-user in portal).

Official articles:
https://support.techsmith.com/hc/en-us/articles/47507877869325-How-do-I-view-activations-or-seats-in-use-for-our-Snagit-or-Camtasia-license
https://support.techsmith.com/hc/en-us/articles/39348008056461-Can-I-Assign-Seats-For-My-Snagit-or-Camtasia-Business-Subscription

- TechSmith does not currently have a license management portal to transfer, audit, or view activations for Snagit and Camtasia.

- Site license is offered if tracking is a burden; contact Sales.
- Seat management is only available for Camtasia Assets, Snagit Assets, Audiate, and Screencast Pro.
- You cannot assign seats for Snagit Business, Camtasia Business, Snagit Legacy, or Camtasia Legacy because those unlock with a software key.
- Named-user licensing for Camtasia/Snagit Business is described as in progress with an uncertain timeline — do not invent a ship date.

Do not tell them to click a Camtasia “Seats” report that does not exist.

Camtasia will not open at all. I double-click it and it flashes then dies. I already reinstalled once. I have a class in two hours.

sources.title: Service TechSmith Agent (TechSmith Agent) Failed to Start
Camtasia Editor Crashes on Startup

diagnosticSteps.prompt: Camtasia 2025 install fails with TechSmith Agent service failed to start. What does that article tell you to install?

options.label: Have them install the latest Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable (x64) from Microsoft's C++ download page, then retry the Camtasia 2025 install.
options.feedback: Service TechSmith Agent Failed to Start tells you to install the latest VC++ x64 redistributable, then retry.

options.label: Have them install the latest .NET Desktop Runtime as the documented TechSmith Agent fix, instead of the Visual C++ x64 redistributable.
options.feedback: The Agent article names Visual C++ Redistributable x64, not a .NET runtime.

options.label: Tell them to turn off UAC permanently because the error mentions privileges, and skip the VC++ install.
options.feedback: The error mentions privileges, but the published fix is still the latest VC++ x64 package, not disabling UAC.

options.label: The startup-crash article also repairs VC++ via https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.x64.exe, which is related, but this ticket's official page is the Agent service article — do not skip it.
options.feedback: Same family of VC++ repair, wrong primary article for this MSI service error.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: What unpublished workaround should you avoid for this Agent service error?

options.label: Do not invent sc.exe create commands for TechSmithAgent. The published fix is the latest VC++ x64 redistributable, then retry setup.
options.feedback: The Agent article does not document a manual service-create command.

options.label: Have them use the Unable to Reach the Activation Service steps (disconnect VPN, proxy) because a failed Agent service is read as a network activation error.
options.feedback: This is an install-time service error, not the activation-service connectivity article.

options.label: Have them uninstall CopyTrans Studio to fix this MSI TechSmith Agent error.
options.feedback: CopyTrans is a Camtasia Editor startup-crash known issue, not this installer service error.

options.label: They may still need sufficient privileges as the error text says, but the article's written fix is still installing VC++ x64 — do not treat a UAC toggle as the whole solution.
options.feedback: Privileges are in the error string; the KB still points at the VC++ x64 package.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: How should you close this TechSmith Agent install error?

options.label: Have them install the latest VC++ x64 redistributable, retry the Camtasia 2025 install, and link Service TechSmith Agent Failed to Start.
options.feedback: That close matches the Agent article.

options.label: Tell them to skip the Agent service with an unpublished installer switch so Camtasia installs without it.
options.feedback: There is no published skip-Agent installer flag; the fix is VC++ x64, then retry.

options.label: Have them reset cache with CamtasiaSupport.app, which is a Mac step, for this Windows MSI error.
options.feedback: CamtasiaSupport.app is macOS Unable to Start; this ticket is a Windows install service error.

options.label: If install later succeeds but Editor still crashes on startup, then use the startup-crash VC++ Repair and restart path.
options.feedback: That related article is for Editor crash-on-startup after a successful install, not this Agent MSI error.

emailCriteria.tone: Exact service error. VC++ x64.
requiredElements: Name TechSmith Agent failed to start
Install latest Visual C++ Redistributable x64
Do not invent sc.exe workarounds
modelReplyHints: VC++ x64, retry install. Link the Agent article.

expectedMacros.rationale: TechSmith Agent service failed during install. Install/Uninstall Errors, not Crash or Training.

Unable to Start, Snagit 2023+.

sources.title: Unable to Start Snagit on Mac
Software Won't Start or Keeps Crashing (Snagit & Camtasia)

diagnosticSteps.prompt: Snagit on Mac shows Unable to Start, but the menu bar sometimes appears. Which Reset Cache path should you use first?

options.label: Because Snagit can open far enough for menus, have them use Help > Support Tool > Reset Cache, confirm Reset, then restart Snagit (2023 and later).
options.feedback: Unable to Start Snagit on Mac documents the Can Open branch as Help > Support Tool > Reset Cache.

options.label: Have them press Win+R and change AnalyticsOptedIn in Registry Editor, using the Windows CrowdStrike Camtasia article on this Mac.
options.feedback: AnalyticsOptedIn is a Windows Camtasia CrowdStrike workaround, not Snagit on Mac.

options.label: Have them uninstall CopyTrans Studio, which is a Camtasia-for-Windows known issue, as the first Snagit Mac step.
options.feedback: CopyTrans is documented on Camtasia Editor Crashes on Startup for Windows, not this Mac Snagit error.

options.label: If Help is not reachable, the Cannot Open path is Show Package Contents → Contents/MacOS/SnagitSupport.app → Reset Cache — use that only if menus are gone; they sometimes have menus, so try Help first.
options.feedback: That is the Cannot Open branch; this customer sometimes sees the menu bar, so Help > Support Tool comes first.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: If they cannot reach Help > Support Tool, what is the documented path?

options.label: Have them open Finder → Applications, right-click Snagit → Show Package Contents, go to Contents/MacOS, open SnagitSupport.app, click Reset Cache, then restart Snagit.
options.feedback: That is the Cannot Open branch in Unable to Start Snagit on Mac.

options.label: Have them delete folders under ~/Library/Application Support that this article does not list, instead of Reset Cache.
options.feedback: This article is Reset Cache only; do not invent extra Library deletions.

options.label: Have them right-click Snagit and Run as administrator, which is a Windows start-hub step.
options.feedback: Run as administrator is Windows; this is Snagit on Mac.

options.label: Camtasia Mac Unable to Start uses CamtasiaSupport.app in a similar package-contents path — do not send those Camtasia steps as the Snagit fix.
options.feedback: The Camtasia Mac article is a sibling pattern; this ticket needs SnagitSupport.app.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: How should you close this Snagit Mac Unable to Start ticket?

options.label: Walk the matching Reset Cache path — Help > Support Tool if menus work, otherwise SnagitSupport.app — and link Unable to Start Snagit on Mac.
options.feedback: That close stays on the Snagit Mac article's two Reset Cache paths.

options.label: Have them reinstall Snagit from a Windows download and run it under a VM as the documented Mac Unable to Start fix.
options.feedback: The documented fix is Reset Cache on the Mac app, not switching them to Windows Snagit.

options.label: Have them enter a new software key to clear Unable to Start, as if this were an activation prompt.
options.feedback: Unable to Start is a cache/launch issue on this article, not a missing-key ticket.

options.label: You may also ask them to restart the Mac and, if Snagit opens, use Check for Updates — those are hub quick fixes, not a replacement for Reset Cache.
options.feedback: Restart and updates are secondary; Reset Cache is the article's written path.

emailCriteria.tone: Mac Reset Cache. Two paths.
requiredElements: Unable to Start on Snagit 2023+
Help > Support Tool > Reset Cache if menus work
Otherwise SnagitSupport.app in Contents/MacOS
modelReplyHints: Help Support Tool Reset Cache, or package SnagitSupport.app.

expectedMacros.rationale: Unable to Start Snagit on Mac. Use the Mac Problem tag — not Windows Snagit macros.

sources.title: VCRUNTIME Error When Launching Snagit
Software Won't Start or Keeps Crashing (Snagit & Camtasia)

diagnosticSteps.prompt: Snagit will not launch because VCRUNTIME140_1.DLL was not found. What is the official first option?

options.label: Have them install the latest Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable packages for Visual Studio 2015, 2017, and 2019, as Option 1 in the VCRUNTIME article.
options.feedback: VCRUNTIME Error When Launching Snagit lists those VC++ packages as Option 1.

options.label: Have them download vcruntime140_1.dll from a third-party DLL site and copy it into System32.
options.feedback: Do not send customers to unofficial DLL downloads; the article starts with the Visual C++ redistributable.

options.label: Have them uninstall CopyTrans Studio, using the Camtasia crash-on-startup article for this Snagit DLL error.
options.feedback: CopyTrans is a Camtasia Windows known issue; this ticket is Snagit VCRUNTIME140_1.DLL.

options.label: After the runtime is installed, you may try restart and Run as administrator from the start hub — do not skip the VC++ packages.
options.feedback: Hub checks are secondary; Option 1 is still the Visual C++ redistributable.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: If installing VC++ is not enough, what else does the VCRUNTIME article document?

options.label: Have them run Command Prompt as administrator, then regsvr32 /u VCRUNTIME140.dll followed by regsvr32 VCRUNTIME140.dll, and if needed run sfc /scannow as Option 3.
options.feedback: Those are Options 2 and 3 in the Snagit VCRUNTIME article, using VCRUNTIME140.dll as written.

options.label: Have them skip VC++ and start with an SFC scan only, because a missing VCRUNTIME DLL is treated as a full Windows image repair first.
options.feedback: SFC is Option 3 after the redistributable and regsvr32; do not skip Option 1.

options.label: Have them run SnagitSupport.app Reset Cache on this Windows PC.
options.feedback: SnagitSupport.app Reset Cache is macOS Unable to Start, not this Windows VCRUNTIME error.

options.label: You may explain that VCRUNTIME140.dll is related to Visual Studio 2015 and that a missing or damaged DLL blocks launch — then still send them through Option 1.
options.feedback: That context is in the article; it does not replace installing the redistributable.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: How should you close this VCRUNTIME ticket?

options.label: Start with the Visual C++ redistributable packages, then regsvr32 and SFC as documented, link the VCRUNTIME article, and do not send them to a third-party DLL download.
options.feedback: That close follows Options 1–3 and the article's warning against unofficial DLL copies.

options.label: Tell them a new software key will replace the missing VCRUNTIME DLL.
options.feedback: This is a runtime DLL launch error, not a licensing or key problem.

options.label: Have them follow the Camtasia EditorInterop.dll article — x64 C++ then reinstall Camtasia — as the fix for this Snagit VCRUNTIME error.
options.feedback: EditorInterop.dll is a Camtasia article; this ticket is Snagit VCRUNTIME140_1.DLL.

options.label: If Snagit opens after the runtime install, have them use Help > Check for Updates.
options.feedback: Updates are fine once it launches; they do not replace the VCRUNTIME article options.

emailCriteria.tone: Quote VCRUNTIME. Official VC++ then article options.
requiredElements: Name VCRUNTIME140_1.DLL / the launch error
Install Visual C++ redistributable packages
Do not download the DLL from a third-party site
modelReplyHints: VC++ packages first. No third-party DLL sites.

expectedMacros.rationale: VCRUNTIME140_1.DLL missing is a Snagit install/runtime error, not Camtasia and not Training.

sources.title: Snagit or Camtasia shows Trial or Expired Trial after I've purchased
Find, Enter, or Recover Your Software Key (Snagit & Camtasia)

diagnosticSteps.prompt: The in-app email already matches the purchase email. What is step 2 in the Trial article?

options.label: Have them go to Help > About Camtasia, click Refresh, then check whether the product shows Licensed instead of Trial.
options.feedback: Snagit or Camtasia shows Trial or Expired Trial after I've purchased lists Help > About → Refresh as step 2.

options.label: Have them enter a 25-character software key, because Individual Create is treated as a key-based SKU after renewal.
options.feedback: Camtasia Individual has no software key; they already signed in with the purchase email.

options.label: Open a billing refund because a Trial badge after renewal means the subscription was not actually charged.
options.feedback: Trial after a valid purchase is a refresh/cache issue in this article, not an automatic failed-charge refund.

options.label: If Refresh fails, have them disconnect any VPN and check firewall or proxy — this PC has no VPN, but a firewall can still block license validation.
options.feedback: Network checks are step 3; step 2 on this ticket is still Help > About → Refresh.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: Refresh did not change the Trial badge. What Windows cleanup does the Trial article document next?

options.label: Have them fully close Camtasia, then delete the files inside the License folder under %LocalAppData%\TechSmith\Camtasia Studio or Camtasia — keep the License folder itself.
options.feedback: Step 4 documents those Camtasia License folder paths and says to delete the files, not the folder.

options.label: Have them delete /Users/Shared/TechSmith, using the Snagit Mac remember-key article on this Windows Camtasia PC.
options.feedback: /Users/Shared/TechSmith is the Mac Snagit key article; this is Windows Camtasia License folder cleanup.

options.label: Have them set Licensed=1 in Registry Editor to force Licensed status, mixing this Trial ticket with a launch-registry workaround.
options.feedback: The Trial article does not document a Licensed registry flag.

options.label: If License folder cleanup is not enough, have them end Camtasia.exe, CamtasiaStudio.exe, and CamtasiaRecorder.exe in Task Manager and clear Public TechSmith License files as step 5.
options.feedback: Deeper cleanup is step 5; on this step, License folder contents under LocalAppData come first.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: Camtasia still shows Trial after the documented Windows steps. How should you close?

options.label: Ask for a screenshot of the Trial UI, the Camtasia version, the Windows version, and which article steps they tried, then contact Technical Support as the Still seeing Trial section says.
options.feedback: That evidence list is the article's documented next step after the cleanup path.

options.label: Have them set AnalyticsOptedIn to 0 to flip Trial to Licensed, mixing the CrowdStrike launch article with this renewal ticket.
options.feedback: AnalyticsOptedIn is the CrowdStrike does-not-open workaround, not a Trial-badge fix.

options.label: Recover or paste a 25-character key for this Individual subscription and have them enter it.
options.feedback: Individual Create has no software key; do not mint or demand one.

options.label: Have them sign in again with the purchase email and re-check Help > About after cleanup.
options.feedback: Sign-in again is in the Still seeing Trial bullets; screenshot plus versions is still the article's close if it stays Trial.

emailCriteria.tone: Correct email → Refresh, then cache. No Individual key.
requiredElements: Help > About → Refresh
Individual has no software key
License folder cleanup if Refresh fails
Link the Trial/Expired Trial article
modelReplyHints: Refresh first. Then License folder. No key.

sources.title: Snagit or Camtasia shows Trial or Expired Trial after I've purchased
Using Camtasia Editor with a Proxy Server/Firewall

diagnosticSteps.prompt: IT will not allow Help > About Refresh to reach the internet. What does the Trial article say about network?

options.label: Tell them a firewall or proxy can block license validation. Have them try another network if possible and work with IT on allowlisting — do not set Licensed=1.
options.feedback: Step 3 of the Trial article covers VPN, firewall, and proxy, and does not document a Licensed registry flag.

options.label: Have them set Licensed=1 in the registry so Camtasia skips network validation.
options.feedback: Licensed=1 is not in the Trial article; proxy and cache steps are.

options.label: Have them paste a 25-character key and skip the network and cache steps, even though this is a signed-in Trial/Expired Trial UI.
options.feedback: Do not skip documented network and License folder cleanup for an Expired Trial badge.

options.label: If IT can allowlist traffic, the proxy article documents hosts such as my.nalpeiron.com and login.techsmith.com on ports 443 and 80.
options.feedback: Using Camtasia Editor with a Proxy Server/Firewall lists those allowlist addresses; they still need the Trial article's cache steps if Refresh stays blocked.

options.label: Have them fully close Camtasia, delete files inside the License folder under %LocalAppData%\TechSmith\Camtasia Studio or Camtasia (not the folder), then if needed clear Public\TechSmith License files and end Camtasia processes in Task Manager.
options.feedback: Trial article steps 4–5 document those Camtasia License folder and process cleanup paths.

options.label: Have them add TechSmith license hosts to the Windows hosts file as the documented proxy workaround, instead of License folder cleanup.
options.feedback: The proxy article uses an allowlist, not a hosts-file workaround, and cache cleanup is still documented.

options.label: Have them delete Program Files\TechSmith entirely as if that were the License folder step.
options.feedback: The article deletes files inside the License folder under LocalAppData, not the Program Files install tree.

options.label: The Trial article also deletes Identity and RegInfo.ini under %programdata%\TechSmith for Snagit or Camtasia if present — stay on those published paths, not invented folders.
options.feedback: Identity/RegInfo is in step 4; Camtasia License folders under LocalAppData are still the primary Camtasia cleanup.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: They asked you to set Licensed=1. How should you close?

options.label: Refuse unpublished Licensed flags. Walk network/allowlist and documented License folder cleanup, then screenshot and escalate to Technical Support if it still shows Expired Trial.
options.feedback: That close matches the Trial article and does not invent a Licensed=1 bypass.

options.label: Have them set AnalyticsOptedIn to 0 to flip Expired Trial to Licensed, mixing the CrowdStrike launch article with this renewal ticket.
options.feedback: AnalyticsOptedIn is the CrowdStrike does-not-open workaround, not a Trial-badge fix.

options.label: Issue a refund so they can repurchase on a home network, instead of walking proxy allowlist and cache steps.
options.feedback: Proxy blocking Refresh is a network/cache issue, not an automatic refund.

options.label: If it still shows Trial, collect a screenshot, product and Windows versions, and which steps were tried, then contact Technical Support.
options.feedback: That evidence list is the article's Still seeing Trial section; still refuse Licensed=1.

requiredElements: Firewall/proxy can block license validation
Do not set Licensed=1
Clear files in the Camtasia License folder under LocalAppData
modelReplyHints: Network/allowlist. Then License folder. No config hacks.

scenarios.crashLog:
macOS Snagit forgets key.

sources.title: Snagit Does Not Remember Key
Snagit: Enter My Software Key

diagnosticSteps.prompt: Snagit forgets the key on Mac reboot. What are the first official steps?

options.label: Have them fully close Snagit, go to /Users/Shared/ in Finder, delete the TechSmith folder, relaunch Snagit, enter the key again, and test after a restart.
options.feedback: Snagit Does Not Remember Key documents closing Snagit, deleting /Users/Shared/TechSmith, re-entering the key, then testing after restart.

options.label: Have them clear %LocalAppData%\TechSmith\Snagit\License, using the Windows Trial article on this Mac.
options.feedback: LocalAppData License folder cleanup is the Windows Trial article; this Mac ticket uses /Users/Shared/TechSmith.

options.label: Tell them the key is burned because Snagit forgot it, so they need a replacement software key from Support.
options.feedback: The article has them re-enter the same key after deleting the Shared TechSmith folder; do not treat a forgotten key as dead.

options.label: After permissions are fixed, have them re-enter the key from Snagit > Enter Software Key.
options.feedback: Enter Software Key is at the end of the article; deleting /Users/Shared/TechSmith comes first.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: It still forgets the key after that folder delete. What about permissions?

options.label: Have them use Get Info → Sharing & Permissions, unlock, and set Read & Write on the Users, Shared, TechSmith, and Snagit folders. After they enter the key, a Registration Key file should appear under /Users/Shared/TechSmith/Snagit.
options.feedback: Those folder privileges and the Registration Key file location are quoted from Snagit Does Not Remember Key.

options.label: Have them change permissions on the macOS System folder instead of the Users, Shared, TechSmith, and Snagit folders the article names.
options.feedback: The article sets Read & Write on Users, Shared, TechSmith, and Snagit — not the System folder.

options.label: Have them set AnalyticsOptedIn in Registry Editor, using the Windows Camtasia CrowdStrike article on this Mac.
options.feedback: AnalyticsOptedIn is a Windows Camtasia launch workaround, not a Mac Snagit key-retention fix.

options.label: Have them test whether the key sticks by restarting the Mac or fully restarting Snagit.
options.feedback: That retention test is step 7; Read & Write on the Shared folders is still required if it forgets again.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: How should you close this Snagit Mac key-retention ticket?

options.label: Walk deleting /Users/Shared/TechSmith, then Read & Write on the Shared folders if it still forgets, and link Snagit Does Not Remember Key.
options.feedback: That close stays on the Mac remember-key article.

options.label: Have them add a license-server entry to the Mac hosts file so the key is treated as an activation-network issue.
options.feedback: This article is Shared-folder delete plus permissions, not a hosts-file activation workaround.

options.label: Tell them this key-based install must never enter a software key and should sign in with an Individual account instead.
options.feedback: This ticket has a perpetual key; the article has them re-enter that key.

options.label: If the UI is Trial rather than a key prompt, use the Trial/Expired Trial article instead of this remember-key path.
options.feedback: Do not mix a Trial badge with a key that will not stick; this ticket is the remember-key symptom.

emailCriteria.tone: Mac Shared folder. Not Windows cache paths.
requiredElements: Go to /Users/Shared/ and remove the TechSmith folder
Re-enter the key
Read & Write permissions if it still forgets
modelReplyHints: Delete /Users/Shared/TechSmith. Then permissions. Re-enter key.

options.feedback: Unable to Start Camtasia Editor on MacOS documents those Mac paths; LocalAppData is Windows-only.

options.label: Give them the Windows License folder path as if %LocalAppData%\TechSmith\Camtasia works in macOS Terminal.
options.feedback: LocalAppData is the Windows Trial article; this customer is on macOS.

options.label: Email a 25-character Individual software key and have them paste it on the Mac.

options.label: After cache and License folder cleanup, have them sign in with the purchase email (Individual).

diagnosticSteps.prompt: If Camtasia will not open, what is the first Mac 2023+ step in that article?

options.label: Have them right-click Camtasia → Show Package Contents, open Contents/MacOS/CamtasiaSupport.app, click Reset Cache, then restart Camtasia.

options.label: Have them use only SnagitSupport.app, saying that tool also resets Camtasia on Mac.

options.label: Have them run Registry Editor and set AnalyticsOptedIn, using the Windows CrowdStrike article on this Mac.
options.feedback: regedit and AnalyticsOptedIn are Windows Camtasia CrowdStrike steps, not macOS.

options.label: Have them delete TechSmith Account Camtasia entries under Login in Keychain Access, and check iCloud if that list is present.
options.feedback: Keychain cleanup is in the same Mac article; Reset Cache via CamtasiaSupport.app is the first 2023+ step when it will not open.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: How should you close this Mac Trial plus Unable to Start ticket?
